figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic illustrations demonstrating the structure of NCM cathode using conductive agents as a) B-CNT and b) PAMPS-CNT, and the eﬀects on Li metal battery operation via chemical crosstalk.

Figure 2. Characterizations of polymer-functionalized CNTs. a) Raman spectroscopy and b) XPS analysis showing the structure of polymer-grafted CNTs. c) EIS-DRT analysis of polymer-grafted CNTs with PEEK washer. 3D laser microscopy of electrodes using conductive agents as d) B-CNT, e) PAM-CNT, and f) PAMPS-CNT. g) Charge-discharge voltage proﬁle of the NCM811||Li cells and h) post-formation EIS-DRT analysis. Long-term cycling stability of NCM811||Li cells at i) high rate (3mAh cm−2, 1 C, 4.3 V cut-oﬀ) and j) high-voltage with high loading (4.5 mAh cm−2, 0.3 C, 4.5 V cut-oﬀ).

Figure 3. Interfacial characterization of cathode and anode surfaces of Li||NCM811 cells. a) XPS analysis of S 2p, P 2p spectra for NCM811 cathodes incorporated with B-CNT or PAMPS-CNT, and b) 3D representation of ToF-SIMS depth proﬁle images of SO3−and PO2– on the NCM811 cathodes after 50 cycles at 0.5 C. TEM images of NCM811 cathodes using c) B-CNT and d) PAMPS-CNT after 50 cycles. The orange and blue squares are FFT images of the corresponding areas in the TEM images. e) XPS analysis of S 2p, F 1s spectra for 40 μm LMA and f) 3D representation of ToF-SIMS depth proﬁle images of SO3−and LiF−on the Li metal anodes at 0.5 C after 50 cycles. Top-view of SEM images of LMA for full cells with g) B-CNT and h) PAMPS-CNT.

Figure 4. Mechanism of the crosstalk eﬀect of PAMPS-CNT. a) EA and CIC analysis of NCM811 cathode before cycle, after 30 cycles, and after 50 cycles. b) HSO3−production mechanism by reaction between PAMPS and LiOH, and their relative energy using DFT calculation. c) Diﬀusion coeﬃcient of Li+, PF6−, and HSO3−. d) HOMO and LUMO energy levels of electrolytes (DEC, EC, FEC, PF6−) and HSO3−. e) Reaction pathway of HSO3−, Li and LiOH for the formation of the SEI layer. f) Schematic illustration of a mechanistic pathway where HSO3−intermediates from PAMPS migrate to the anode and contribute to the formation of a stable SEI layer.

Figure 5. Electrochemical kinetics of PAMPS-CNT electrode. a) Changes in the internal resistance as a function of voltage during charge and discharge using GITT measurement. b) Measurement of diﬀusion coeﬃcient using voltage change with PITT analysis. EIS-DRT measurements on NCM811-based three-electrode cells incorporated c) B-CNT and d) PAMPS-CNT.

Figure 6. Electrochemical performance of Li||NCM811 cells using PAMPS-CNT at various conditions. a) Fabrication high-loading NCM811 cathodes using B-CNT and PAMPS-CNT. b) Cycling performance of Li||NCM811 cells with PAMPS-CNT based NCM811 cathode. (37.4– 58.4 mg cm−2).c) Long- term cycling performance using S-free advanced electrolyte optimized for Li metal stability, (6.0 mAh cm−2, 0.2 C/0.3 C for charge/discharge, 4.5 V cut-oﬀ) and d) consequent cell voltage proﬁle. e) Cycle retention of Bi-stack pouch cell with 8.5 mAh cm−2 NCM811 cathode using PAMPS-CNT and f) corresponding voltage proﬁle. g) The performance of high-energy-density Li metal pouch cells with high loading cathode (more than 2.0 mAh cm−2) in reported literature and this work.
